extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 challenging samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Chen, Lin, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, and Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline. The authors choose two benchmarks focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge for sample collection. They employ two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs sizing 20B or larger as inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage, evaluate the sample pool, document hit frequency for each sample, and retain only samples with hit counts of two or fewer. After coarse filtering reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607, three experts manually reviewed samples to ensure visual dependency, comprehensive capability coverage, and advanced multi-modal difficulty, then manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source consists of samples selected from six existing benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark samples were filtered using an automated pipeline based on LLM inspector hit counts, excluding samples answerable by more than 2 of 8 LLMs. Coarsely filtered samples were then grouped into four difficulty categories using hit counts from 16 LVLMs: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection considered diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors developed an automated coarse filtering pipeline. Open-source LLM inspectors were applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. They evaluated the sample pool, recorded hit frequency for each sample, and retained only samples with hit counts of two or fewer, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 before manual review.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure each sample’s answer should be based on understanding visual content, selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions, and most samples require advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. The final benchmark is organized into 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To expedite manual selection with varying difficulty levels, the authors tallied hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final curation considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: In the future, the authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that inappropriate questions and data leakage can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLMs. It states that for research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage so models are evaluated on their true ability to integrate and interpret multi-modal data rather than memorize specific samples.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two benchmark biases/issues in existing evaluations: many samples do not require visual content because answers can be inferred from text or world knowledge, and unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. These issues can unfairly inflate benchmark performance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Even on MMStar, the best evaluated model scores under 60 on average. The paper also notes that current evaluations can be unfair due to visual-unnecessary samples and data leakage, and future work is needed to maintain visual dependency and reduce accidental leakage.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models’ multi-modal capabilities across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, and for assessing actual multi-modal performance gain and data leakage using the proposed MG and ML metrics.
